recovery_balance.meaning: HRV z-score minus load z-score; below 0 = load outpacing recovery

aerobic_decoupling_pct.note: first-half vs second-half efficiency drift; under 5% = aerobically sound

drivers: HRV is +4.4 ms above baseline (68.5 vs 64.1 ms), indicating solid parasympathetic resilience
Resting HR has declined -1.2 bpm (50.2 vs 51.5 bpm), supporting improved cardiovascular recovery
ACWR = 0.8 — in optimal range, signaling no acute overload
Recovery balance = +2.24 (well above 0), meaning HRV is currently outpacing load stress
But sleep remains critically low: 4.6 hrs/night avg, with 15 nights <7h in last 14 days — a major limiting factor for tissue repair and neural adaptation
readiness.guidance: You’re physiologically prepared for moderate training, but chronic sleep debt undermines adaptation — prioritize sleep consolidation before adding intensity.

monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp reduction in volume and intensity versus last month, with pace slowing and zone distribution shifting heavily toward Z3 — likely reflecting fatigue management or intentional deload, but not yet supported by recovery metrics showing full readiness.
monthly_review.highlight: Cadence jumped +35 spm this month (153 vs 118 spm), the largest single-month shift in the 5-month history — suggesting either conscious form work or compensatory mechanics due to fatigue or reduced stride length.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 82.4 km would require 55.3 km across 8 remaining sessions — ~6.9 km/session — which contradicts current readiness (low sleep, declining efficiency, elevated aerobic TE in recent runs) and risks reinforcing fatigue. Chasing this number is inadvisable; focus instead on quality, consistency, and sleep recovery.

insights.title: Chronic sleep debt correlates with worsened running economy
insights.body: Despite stable VO2max (+2.3 from baseline) and improving HRV, running economy has deteriorated from 13.42 (May) to 13.9 (Aug), while sleep remains stuck at 4.6 hrs/night — below the 6.5–7.5 hr threshold required for glycogen resynthesis and neuromuscular recovery.

insights.title: Low ACWR masks underlying aerobic fragility
insights.body: ACWR = 0.8 suggests underloading, yet aerobic decoupling median is 7.11% (above the 5% threshold), and latest decoupling is 4.8% — borderline. This indicates the aerobic system is struggling to maintain efficiency *even at low loads*, likely due to cumulative sleep debt and incomplete recovery between sessions.

insights.title: Cadence surge coincides with reduced stride length and higher vertical oscillation
insights.body: Cadence rose +35 spm while stride length dropped (e.g., 83.64 cm on 8/7 vs 79.52 cm on 8/2) and vertical oscillation increased (7.9 → 8.0 cm); this inefficient compensation pattern appears during high-fatigue windows (e.g., post-12 km long run on 8/9), suggesting neural fatigue rather than form mastery.

insights.title: Training Readiness score (33) is disconnected from objective recovery metrics
insights.body: Training Readiness is low (33), yet HRV is elevated (+4.4 ms), resting HR is down (-1.2 bpm), and recovery balance is strongly positive (+2.24) — indicating Garmin’s algorithm may be over-penalizing recent low-volume, high-cadence sessions or sleep debt without weighting HRV appropriately.

recommendations.action: Sleep hygiene protocol: Lights out by 22:00, no screens after 21:30, 30-min wind-down ritual — for all 7 days
recommendations.reason: Sleep debt (4.6 hrs/night, 15/14 nights <7h) is the dominant limiter for recovery, efficiency, and injury resilience — no training stimulus will consolidate without it.

recommendations.action: Zone 2 run: 5 km, HR ≤135 bpm, cadence capped at 155 spm, on Tuesday — stop if vertical oscillation exceeds 7.5 cm (per Garmin real-time metric)
recommendations.reason: Cadence has become dissociated from efficiency; this session reinforces aerobic pacing while preventing compensatory bounce — aligned with current ACWR=0.8 and adequate HRV.

recommendations.action: Active recovery walk: 45 min, HR ≤115 bpm, barefoot on grass if possible, on Thursday
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time increased slightly (299 → 301 ms) and vertical oscillation is rising (7.8 → 8.0 cm); low-load proprioceptive input supports neuromuscular reset without adding systemic stress.

risk_flags.evidence: Vertical oscillation increased from 5.5–6.6 cm (7/31–8/2) to 7.8–8.0 cm (8/7–8/13); cadence rose +35 spm while stride length decreased and aerobic TE rose from 1.9 to 3.5 across same period
risk_flags.action: Pause all intervals and hill work until vertical oscillation stabilizes ≤7.2 cm for 3 consecutive runs

risk_flags.evidence: Running economy declined from 13.42 (May) to 13.9 (Aug) while sleep remains 4.6 hrs/night and 15 of last 14 nights were <7h
risk_flags.action: Prioritize sleep extension before increasing weekly TRIMP beyond 460

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish efficient movement patterns under low physiological stress by anchoring cadence, minimizing vertical oscillation, and leveraging sleep as the primary adaptation lever — not volume or intensity.
suggested_sessions: Zone 2 easy run with cadence cap
